sanskrit: tataḥ prahasya nakulaś caturbhiś caturo raṇe jaghāna niśitais tīkṣṇaiḥ satyasenasya vājinaḥ
english: Then Nakula, laughing, slew with four keen, sharp arrows the four horses of Satyasena in the battle.

sanskrit: tataḥ saṃdhāya nārācaṃ rukmapuṅkhaṃ śilāśitam dhanuś ciccheda rājendra satyasenasya pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then, fitting to his bow an iron shaft, gold-feathered and whetted on stone, the son of Pāṇḍu, O lord of kings, cut asunder the bow of Satyasena.

sanskrit: athānyaṃ ratham āsthāya dhanur ādāya cāparam satyasenaḥ suṣeṇaś ca pāṇḍavaṃ paryadhāvatām
english: Then mounting another chariot and taking up another bow, Satyasena and Suṣeṇa together rushed upon the son of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: avidhyat tāv asaṃbhrāntau mādrīputraḥ pratāpavān dvābhyāṃ dvābhyāṃ mahārāja śarābhyāṃ raṇamūrdhani
english: Unflinching, the valiant son of Mādrī pierced them both, O great king, with two arrows each at the head of the battle.

sanskrit: suṣeṇas tu tataḥ kruddhaḥ pāṇḍavasya mahad dhanuḥ ciccheda prahasan yuddhe kṣurapreṇa mahārathaḥ
english: Then Suṣeṇa, enraged, that mighty car-warrior, laughing, cut the great bow of the son of Pāṇḍu in the fight with a razor-edged arrow.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya nakulaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ suṣeṇaṃ pañcabhir viddhvā dhvajam ekena cicchide
english: Then, taking up another bow, Nakula, beside himself with rage, pierced Suṣeṇa with five arrows and cut down his banner with one.

sanskrit: satyasenasya ca dhanur hastāvāpaṃ ca māriṣa ciccheda tarasā yuddhe tata uccukruśur janāḥ
english: And the bow of Satyasena and his leather hand-guard, O sire, he swiftly cut through in the fight; thereupon the people raised a shout.

sanskrit: athānyad dhanur ādāya vegaghnaṃ bhārasādhanam śaraiḥ saṃchādayām āsa samantāt pāṇḍunandanam
english: Then, taking up another bow that could break the onrush and bear a heavy strain, he covered the son of Pāṇḍu with arrows on every side.

sanskrit: saṃnivārya tu tān bāṇān nakulaḥ paravīrahā satyasenaṃ suṣeṇaṃ ca dvābhyāṃ dvābhyām avidhyata
english: But Nakula, slayer of hostile heroes, having warded off those arrows, pierced Satyasena and Suṣeṇa with two shafts each.

sanskrit: tāv enaṃ pratyavidhyetāṃ pṛthak pṛthag ajihmagaiḥ sārathiṃ cāsya rājendra śarair vivyadhatuḥ śitaiḥ
english: Those two pierced him in return, each separately, with straight-flying shafts, and they wounded his charioteer, O lord of kings, with whetted arrows.

sanskrit: satyaseno ratheṣāṃ tu nakulasya dhanus tathā pṛthak śarābhyāṃ ciccheda kṛtahastaḥ pratāpavān
english: And Satyasena, valiant and deft of hand, cut with two separate arrows the chariot-pole and the bow of Nakula.

sanskrit: sa rathe 'tirathas tiṣṭhan rathaśaktiṃ parāmṛśat svarṇadaṇḍām akuṇṭhāgrāṃ tailadhautāṃ sunirmalām
english: That foremost of car-warriors, standing in his chariot, laid hold of a chariot-lance with a golden shaft, of unblunted point, oil-washed and gleaming clean.

sanskrit: lelihānām iva vibho nāgakanyāṃ mahāviṣām samudyamya ca cikṣepa satyasenasya saṃyuge
english: Resembling, O lord, a serpent-maiden of deadly venom flickering her tongue, he raised it high and hurled it at Satyasena in the encounter.

sanskrit: sā tasya hṛdayaṃ saṃkhye bibheda śatadhā nṛpa sa papāta rathād bhūmau gatasattvo 'lpacetanaḥ
english: It split his heart asunder a hundredfold in the battle, O king; bereft of life and barely conscious, he fell from his chariot to the ground.

sanskrit: bhrātaraṃ nihataṃ dṛṣṭvā suṣeṇaḥ krodhamūrchitaḥ abhyavarṣac charais tūrṇaṃ padātiṃ pāṇḍunandanam
english: Seeing his brother slain, Suṣeṇa, beside himself with rage, swiftly rained arrows upon the son of Pāṇḍu, who was now on foot.

sanskrit: nakulaṃ virathaṃ dṛṣṭvā draupadeyo mahābalaḥ sutasomo 'bhidudrāva parīpsan pitaraṃ raṇe
english: Seeing Nakula deprived of his chariot, the mighty Sutasoma, son of Draupadī, rushed forward, eager to save his father in the battle.

sanskrit: tato 'dhiruhya nakulaḥ sutasomasya taṃ ratham śuśubhe bharataśreṣṭho giristha iva kesarī so 'nyat kārmukam ādāya suṣeṇaṃ samayodhayat
english: Then mounting that chariot of Sutasoma, Nakula, foremost of the Bharatas, shone like a lion upon a mountain; taking up another bow, he gave battle to Suṣeṇa.

sanskrit: tāv ubhau śaravarṣābhyāṃ samāsādya parasparam parasparavadhe yatnaṃ cakratuḥ sumahārathau
english: Those two mighty car-warriors, closing upon each other with showers of arrows, each strove hard to slay the other.

sanskrit: suṣeṇas tu tataḥ kruddhaḥ pāṇḍavaṃ viśikhais tribhiḥ sutasomaṃ ca viṃśatyā bāhvor urasi cārpayat
english: Then Suṣeṇa, enraged, planted three shafts in the son of Pāṇḍu and twenty in the arms and chest of Sutasoma.

sanskrit: tataḥ kruddho mahārāja nakulaḥ paravīrahā śarais tasya diśaḥ sarvāś chādayām āsa vīryavān
english: Then, enraged, O great king, the valiant Nakula, slayer of hostile heroes, covered all the quarters about him with arrows.

sanskrit: tato gṛhītvā tīkṣṇāgram ardhacandraṃ sutejanam sa vegayuktaṃ cikṣepa karṇaputrasya saṃyuge
english: Then, taking up a keen-pointed, well-sharpened crescent-headed arrow, he hurled it with great force at the son of Karṇa in the encounter.

sanskrit: tasya tena śiraḥ kāyāj jahāra nṛpasattama paśyatāṃ sarvasainyānāṃ tad adbhutam ivābhavat
english: With it he severed his head from his body, O best of kings, before the eyes of all the troops; that was as a thing of wonder.

sanskrit: sa hataḥ prāpatad rājan nakulena mahātmanā nadīvegād ivārugṇas tīrajaḥ pādapo mahān
english: Slain by the great-souled Nakula, O king, he fell down like a great tree growing on a bank, uprooted by the river's flood.

sanskrit: karṇaputravadhaṃ dṛṣṭvā nakulasya ca vikramam pradudrāva bhayāt senā tāvakī bharatarṣabha
english: Seeing the slaying of Karṇa's son and the prowess of Nakula, your army fled in terror, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: tāṃ tu senāṃ mahārāja madrarājaḥ pratāpavān apālayad raṇe śūraḥ senāpatir ariṃdamaḥ
english: But that army, O great king, the valiant king of the Madras, the heroic commander and tamer of foes, protected in the battle.

sanskrit: vibhīs tasthau mahārāja vyavasthāpya ca vāhinīm siṃhanādaṃ bhṛśaṃ kṛtvā dhanuḥśabdaṃ ca dāruṇam
english: Fearless he stood, O great king, having rallied the host, raising a great lion's roar and a terrible twang of his bow.

sanskrit: tāvakāḥ samare rājan rakṣitā dṛḍhadhanvanā pratyudyayur arātīṃs te samantād vigatavyathāḥ
english: Your men in the battle, O king, guarded by that firm-bowed warrior, advanced against their foes on every side, their anguish gone.

sanskrit: madrarājaṃ maheṣvāsaṃ parivārya samantataḥ sthitā rājan mahāsenā yoddhukāmāḥ samantataḥ
english: Surrounding the great archer, the king of the Madras, on every side, the mighty host stood, O king, eager for battle all around.

sanskrit: sātyakir bhīmasenaś ca mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau yudhiṣṭhiraṃ puraskṛtya hrīniṣedham ariṃdamam
english: Sātyaki and Bhīmasena, and the two sons of Mādrī, the Pāṇḍavas, placing at their head Yudhiṣṭhira, the tamer of foes who shrank from no shameful deed—

sanskrit: parivārya raṇe vīrāḥ siṃhanādaṃ pracakrire bāṇaśabdaravāṃś cogrān kṣveḍāṃś ca vividhān dadhuḥ
english: those heroes, ranging themselves about him in the battle, raised a lion's roar and uttered fierce twangs of bowstrings and shouts of many kinds.

sanskrit: tathaiva tāvakāḥ sarve madrādhipatim añjasā parivārya susaṃrabdhāḥ punar yuddham arocayan
english: Even so all your men, gathering swiftly about the lord of the Madras, full of fury, longed once more for the fight.

sanskrit: tataḥ pravavṛte yuddhaṃ bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhanam tāvakānāṃ pareṣāṃ ca mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam
english: Then began a battle that swelled the terror of the timid, in which both your men and the foe made death their only turning-back.

sanskrit: yathā devāsuraṃ yuddhaṃ pūrvam āsīd viśāṃ pate abhītānāṃ tathā rājan yamarāṣṭravivardhanam
english: As of old, O lord of peoples, was the battle of gods and asuras, so was this fight of fearless men, O king, that swelled the realm of Yama.

sanskrit: tataḥ kapidhvajo rājan hatvā saṃśaptakān raṇe abhyadravata tāṃ senāṃ kauravīṃ pāṇḍunandanaḥ
english: Then the ape-bannered son of Pāṇḍu, O king, having slain the saṃśaptakas in the battle, charged against that Kaurava army.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavāḥ śeṣā dhṛṣṭadyumnapurogamāḥ abhyadhāvanta tāṃ senāṃ visṛjantaḥ śitāñ śarān
english: Even so the remaining Pāṇḍavas, with Dhṛṣṭadyumna at their head, rushed against that army, loosing whetted arrows.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavair avakīrṇānāṃ saṃmohaḥ samajāyata na ca jajñur anīkāni diśo vā pradiśas tathā
english: Among those scattered by the Pāṇḍavas a great bewilderment arose; they could no longer tell their own divisions, nor the cardinal points, nor the quarters between.

sanskrit: āpūryamāṇā niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ pāṇḍavacoditaiḥ hatapravīrā vidhvastā kīryamāṇā samantataḥ kauravy avadhyata camūḥ pāṇḍuputrair mahārathaiḥ
english: Filled with whetted arrows sped by the Pāṇḍavas, its foremost warriors slain, shattered and scattered on every side, the Kaurava host was slaughtered by the mighty car-warriors, the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: tathaiva pāṇḍavī senā śarai rājan samantataḥ raṇe 'hanyata putrais te śataśo 'tha sahasraśaḥ
english: Even so the Pāṇḍava army, O king, was struck with arrows on every side in the battle by your sons, by hundreds and by thousands.

sanskrit: te sene bhṛśasaṃtapte vadhyamāne parasparam vyākule samapadyetāṃ varṣāsu saritāv iva
english: Those two armies, sorely afflicted and slaughtering each other, fell into confusion, like two rivers in the rainy season.

sanskrit: āviveśa tatas tīvraṃ tāvakānāṃ mahad bhayam pāṇḍavānāṃ ca rājendra tathābhūte mahāhave
english: Then a sharp and mighty terror entered both your men and the Pāṇḍavas, O lord of kings, in that great battle so engaged.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca tasmin vilulite sainye vadhyamāne parasparam dravamāṇeṣu yodheṣu ninadatsu ca dantiṣu
english: Saṃjaya said: When that host was thrown into disorder and the warriors slew one another, the fighters fleeing and the elephants trumpeting—

sanskrit: kūjatāṃ stanatāṃ caiva padātīnāṃ mahāhave vidruteṣu mahārāja hayeṣu bahudhā tadā
english: the foot-soldiers wailing and groaning in that great battle, and the horses, O great king, scattering in all directions then—

sanskrit: prakṣaye dāruṇe jāte saṃhāre sarvadehinām nānāśastrasamāvāpe vyatiṣaktarathadvipe
english: a terrible destruction having arisen, a slaughter of all embodied beings, with a clash of weapons of every kind, the chariots and elephants entangled together—

sanskrit: harṣaṇe yuddhaśauṇḍānāṃ bhīrūṇāṃ bhayavardhane gāhamāneṣu yodheṣu parasparavadhaiṣiṣu
english: a thing of joy to those drunk with war, and of swelling terror to the timid, as the warriors plunged in, each seeking to slay the other—

sanskrit: prāṇādāne mahāghore vartamāne durodare saṃgrāme ghorarūpe tu yamarāṣṭravivardhane
english: while that most dreadful taking of life went on, like a desperate game of dice, in a battle of terrible aspect that swelled the realm of Yama—

sanskrit: pāṇḍavās tāvakaṃ sainyaṃ vyadhaman niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ tathaiva tāvakā yodhā jaghnuḥ pāṇḍavasainikān
english: the Pāṇḍavas scattered your host with whetted arrows, and even so your warriors slew the soldiers of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tathā vartamāne yuddhe bhīrubhayāvahe pūrvāhṇe caiva saṃprāpte bhāskarodayanaṃ prati
english: While that battle, striking terror into the fearful, was thus being waged, and the forenoon had come, near the rising of the sun—

sanskrit: labdhalakṣāḥ pare rājan rakṣitāś ca mahātmanā ayodhayaṃs tava balaṃ mṛtyuṃ kṛtvā nivartanam
english: the foes, sure of their aim and guarded by that great-souled one, gave battle to your forces, making death their only turning-back.

sanskrit: balibhiḥ pāṇḍavair dṛptair labdhalakṣaiḥ prahāribhiḥ kauravy asīdat pṛtanā mṛgīvāgnisamākulā
english: Before the strong, proud, sure-aiming, hard-striking Pāṇḍavas, the Kaurava army sank down, distraught like a doe in a forest fire.

sanskrit: tāṃ dṛṣṭvā sīdatīṃ senāṃ paṅke gām iva durbalām ujjihīrṣus tadā śalyaḥ prāyāt pāṇḍucamūṃ prati
english: Seeing that army sinking like a feeble cow in the mire, Śalya, wishing to rescue it, then advanced against the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: madrarājas tu saṃkruddho gṛhītvā dhanur uttamam abhyadravata saṃgrāme pāṇḍavān ātatāyinaḥ
english: And the king of the Madras, greatly enraged, taking up his excellent bow, rushed in the battle against the Pāṇḍavas with bows drawn for the kill.

sanskrit: pāṇḍavāś ca mahārāja samare jitakāśinaḥ madrarājaṃ samāsādya vivyadhur niśitaiḥ śaraiḥ
english: And the Pāṇḍavas, O great king, wearing the look of conquerors in the battle, closing upon the king of the Madras, pierced him with whetted arrows.

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraśatais tīkṣṇair madrarājo mahābalaḥ ardayām āsa tāṃ senāṃ dharmarājasya paśyataḥ
english: Then with hundreds of keen arrows the mighty king of the Madras tormented that army, while the King of Righteousness looked on.

sanskrit: prādurāsaṃs tato rājan nānārūpāṇy anekaśaḥ cacāla śabdaṃ kurvāṇā mahī cāpi saparvatā
english: Then, O king, portents of many kinds appeared in their multitudes, and the earth with its mountains trembled, giving forth a roar.

sanskrit: sadaṇḍaśūlā dīptāgrāḥ śīryamāṇāḥ samantataḥ ulkā bhūmiṃ divaḥ petur āhatya ravimaṇḍalam
english: With trailing shafts like spears and blazing tips, breaking apart on every side, meteors fell from the sky to the earth, striking the disk of the sun.

sanskrit: mṛgāś ca māhiṣāś cāpi pakṣiṇaś ca viśāṃ pate apasavyaṃ tadā cakruḥ senāṃ te bahuśo nṛpa
english: And deer and buffaloes and birds, O lord of peoples, then circled the army, keeping it on their left, again and again, O king.

sanskrit: tatas tad yuddham atyugram abhavat saṃghacāriṇām tathā sarvāṇy anīkāni saṃnipatya janādhipa abhyayuḥ kauravā rājan pāṇḍavānām anīkinīm
english: Then most fierce grew the battle of those who moved in massed array; and all the divisions joining together, O lord of men, the Kauravas, O king, advanced against the host of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: śalyas tu śaravarṣeṇa varṣann iva sahasradṛk abhyavarṣad adīnātmā kuntīputraṃ yudhiṣṭhiram
english: And Śalya, of undaunted soul, raining a shower of arrows like the thousand-eyed Indra pouring rain, deluged Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ śaraiś cāpi rukmapuṅkhaiḥ śilāśitaḥ draupadeyāṃs tathā sarvān mādrīputrau ca pāṇḍavau
english: And with arrows gold-feathered and whetted on stone he struck Bhīmasena, and all the sons of Draupadī, and the two sons of Mādrī, the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ ca śaineyaṃ śikhaṇḍinam athāpi ca ekaikaṃ daśabhir bāṇair vivyādha ca mahābalaḥ tato 'sṛjad bāṇavarṣaṃ gharmānte maghavān iva
english: And Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and the grandson of Śini, and Śikhaṇḍin too—each one the mighty warrior pierced with ten arrows; then he loosed a shower of arrows, as Maghavan pours rain at the end of the hot season.

sanskrit: tataḥ prabhadrakā rājan somakāś ca sahasraśaḥ patitāḥ pātyamānāś ca dṛśyante śalyasāyakaiḥ
english: Then the Prabhadrakas, O king, and the Somakas by the thousand were seen fallen and falling beneath the shafts of Śalya.

sanskrit: bhramarāṇām iva vrātāḥ śalabhānām iva vrajāḥ hrādinya iva meghebhyaḥ śalyasya nyapatañ śarāḥ
english: Like swarms of bees, like flights of locusts, like lightnings from the clouds, the arrows of Śalya fell down.

sanskrit: dviradās turagāś cārtāḥ pattayo rathinas tathā śalyasya bāṇair nyapatan babhramur vyanadaṃs tathā
english: Elephants and horses in distress, and foot-soldiers and car-warriors alike, fell beneath the arrows of Śalya, reeled, and cried aloud.

sanskrit: āviṣṭa iva madreśo manyunā pauruṣeṇa ca prācchādayad arīn saṃkhye kālasṛṣṭa ivāntakaḥ vinardamāno madreśo meghahrādo mahābalaḥ
english: As if possessed, the lord of the Madras, with wrath and manly might, covered his foes in the battle like the Ender sent forth by Time; roaring like a thunder-cloud, mighty was the lord of the Madras.

sanskrit: sā vadhyamānā śalyena pāṇḍavānām anīkinī ajātaśatruṃ kaunteyam abhyadhāvad yudhiṣṭhiram
english: That host of the Pāṇḍavas, slaughtered by Śalya, ran toward Yudhiṣṭhira, the son of Kuntī, whose foe was yet unborn.

sanskrit: tāṃ samarpya tataḥ saṃkhye laghuhastaḥ śitaiḥ śaraiḥ śaravarṣeṇa mahatā yudhiṣṭhiram apīḍayat
english: Having flung that host upon him in the battle, the deft-handed one with whetted arrows, with a great shower of shafts, afflicted Yudhiṣṭhira.

sanskrit: tam āpatantaṃ pattyaśvaiḥ kruddho rājā yudhiṣṭhiraḥ avārayac charais tīkṣṇair mattaṃ dvipam ivāṅkuśaiḥ
english: As he bore down with foot and horse, the enraged king Yudhiṣṭhira held him back with keen arrows, as one checks a rutting elephant with goads.

sanskrit: tasya śalyaḥ śaraṃ ghoraṃ mumocāśīviṣopamam so 'bhyavidhyan mahātmānaṃ vegenābhyapatac ca gām
english: At him Śalya loosed a dreadful arrow like a venomous serpent; it pierced the great-souled one and then with force buried itself in the earth.

sanskrit: tato vṛkodaraḥ kruddhaḥ śalyaṃ vivyādha saptabhiḥ pañcabhiḥ sahadevas tu nakulo daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ
english: Then Vṛkodara, enraged, pierced Śalya with seven arrows, and Sahadeva with five, and Nakula with ten.

sanskrit: draupadeyāś ca śatrughnaṃ śūram ārtāyaniṃ śaraiḥ abhyavarṣan mahābhāgaṃ meghā iva mahīdharam
english: And the sons of Draupadī rained arrows upon the foe-slaying hero, the illustrious son of Ṛtāyana, as clouds upon a mountain.

sanskrit: tato dṛṣṭvā tudyamānaṃ śalyaṃ pārthaiḥ samantataḥ kṛtavarmā kṛpaś caiva saṃkruddhāv abhyadhāvatām
english: Then, seeing Śalya being struck by the sons of Pṛthā on every side, Kṛtavarman and Kṛpa, both greatly enraged, rushed forward.

sanskrit: ulūkaś ca patatrī ca śakuniś cāpi saubalaḥ smayamānaś ca śanakair aśvatthāmā mahārathaḥ tava putrāś ca kārtsnyena jugupuḥ śalyam āhave
english: And Ulūka and Patatrin, and Śakuni the son of Subala, and Aśvatthāman the mighty car-warrior, smiling softly, and your sons in their entirety, guarded Śalya in the battle.

sanskrit: bhīmasenaṃ tribhir viddhvā kṛtavarmā śilīmukhaiḥ bāṇavarṣeṇa mahatā kruddharūpam avārayat
english: Kṛtavarman, having pierced Bhīmasena with three sharp arrows, held him back, wrath-faced as he was, with a great shower of shafts.

sanskrit: dhṛṣṭadyumnaṃ kṛpaḥ kruddho bāṇavarṣair apīḍayat draupadeyāṃś ca śakunir yamau ca drauṇir abhyayāt
english: Kṛpa, enraged, afflicted Dhṛṣṭadyumna with showers of arrows; Śakuni assailed the sons of Draupadī, and the son of Droṇa fell upon the twins.

sanskrit: duryodhano yudhāṃ śreṣṭhāv āhave keśavārjunau samabhyayād ugratejāḥ śaraiś cābhyahanad balī
english: Duryodhana of fierce energy advanced against those two foremost of warriors in the battle, Keśava and Arjuna, and the mighty one struck them with arrows.

sanskrit: evaṃ dvaṃdvaśatāny āsaṃs tvadīyānāṃ paraiḥ saha ghorarūpāṇi citrāṇi tatra tatra viśāṃ pate
english: Thus there were hundreds of single combats between your men and the foe, of terrible aspect and wondrous to behold, here and there, O lord of peoples.

sanskrit: ṛśyavarṇāñ jaghānāśvān bhojo bhīmasya saṃyuge so 'vatīrya rathopasthād dhatāśvaḥ pāṇḍunandanaḥ kālo daṇḍam ivodyamya gadāpāṇir ayudhyata
english: The Bhoja slew the antelope-colored horses of Bhīma in the encounter; and the son of Pāṇḍu, his horses slain, descending from the floor of his chariot, mace in hand, raising it like Death lifting his rod, fought on.

sanskrit: pramukhe sahadevasya jaghānāśvāṃś ca madrarāṭ tataḥ śalyasya tanayaṃ sahadevo 'sināvadhīt
english: Before the face of Sahadeva the king of the Madras slew his horses; thereupon Sahadeva slew the son of Śalya with his sword.

sanskrit: gautamaḥ punar ācāryo dhṛṣṭadyumnam ayodhayat asaṃbhrāntam asaṃbhrānto yatnavān yatnavattaram
english: The preceptor of Gautama's line again gave battle to Dhṛṣṭadyumna—the unflinching against the unflinching, the diligent against the more diligent still.

sanskrit: draupadeyāṃs tathā vīrān ekaikaṃ daśabhiḥ śaraiḥ avidhyad ācāryasuto nātikruddhaḥ smayann iva
english: And the heroic sons of Draupadī—each one with ten arrows the son of the preceptor pierced, not greatly enraged, as though with a smile.
